path.title: FIU Admissions - First Year Pathways (admission standards)

test_policy.notes: 'All freshman applicants are required to submit an SAT, ACT or CLT score for admissions consideration. This includes in-state, out of state and international students.' The ACT Science section is optional since April 2025 (composite = English, math and reading). Admission also depends on meeting the Florida Board of Governors college-readiness requirement through SAT/ACT Verbal/Reading and English subscores plus an appropriate GPA. Scores received after the deadline are not considered for the term or for scholarships.

requirements.supplemental_essays: None listed on the first-year checklist (Common App only).
requirements.notes: First-year applicants apply only through the Common App (no separate FIU application) with a $30 fee or an SAT/ACT fee waiver. Required: official transcripts sent directly from every school attended (certified English translations for other languages, plus the original), SAT/ACT/CLT scores (SAT code 5206, ACT code 0776), and residency documentation; applications are not reviewed until complete. Admission decisions are 'based on your grade point average (GPA) combined with your SAT, ACT or CLT scores'; the checklist lists no essay or recommendation requirement, though the CDS (C7) marks the essay and recommendations 'Considered' and the interview 'Not Considered'. FIU assigns each applicant a best-fit pathway (Fall Direct, Early Fall Direct, Spring Direct, START, Golden Scholars); Fall Direct is the most selective and Early Fall Direct starts in June. Applications open August 1.

deadlines.label: Early Action: complete application with documents, Fall 2027 (also Early Fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: FIU's table lists Early Action under 'Complete App with Docs: November 2, 2026; Notification: December 10, 2026; Deposit: May 1, 2027', same dates for Early Fall and Fall 2027. Non-binding. The scholarships page says Nov. 2, 2026 is the merit-scholarship date for applicants at Florida high schools.

deadlines.label: All first-year applicants: complete application with documents, Fall 2027 (also Early Fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Notification January 21, 2027; deposit May 1, 2027. The scholarships page gives December 16, 2026 as the date for merit scholarship and non-resident tuition waiver consideration for applicants at out-of-state or overseas high schools (complete application, fee or waiver, and official SAT/ACT/CLT scores).

deadlines.label: Final deadline: complete application with documents, Fall 2027 (also Early Fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Last decisions April 2, 2027. No separate international deadline is listed on the international pages; the same first-year table applies.

deadlines.label: Merit scholarship / non-resident tuition waiver consideration for applicants at out-of-state or overseas high schools
deadlines.notes: Complete application, application fee or waiver and official SAT/ACT/CLT scores by this date; no separate scholarship application. Florida high school applicants use Nov. 2, 2026. The page header says 'Early Fall/ Fall 2026' but the dates match the Fall 2027 application table. International students need an F-1 (or other eligible) visa.

deadlines.label: Deposit deadline (Early Action, all first-year and final deadline applicants)

english_policy.waiver_notes: International first-time-in-college applicants are not required to submit TOEFL or IELTS for direct admission; applicants from non-English-speaking countries must still show English proficiency, which FIU assesses through the Florida Board of Governors college-readiness requirement (SAT or ACT Verbal/Reading and English subscores plus the appropriate GPA). The pages list no TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE or Cambridge minimums for freshmen. Quote (international freshman page, step 4): 'For direct admission to FIU, international first time in college students are not required to submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.' The first-year page's generic line 'International students must submit English language proficiency exams and other documents to apply to FIU' prints no scores, so it is not treated as a minimum.

aid.notes: Policy left blank because the sources disagree: CDS H6 ticks both 'institutional need-based aid is available' and 'institutional aid is not available' for nonresidents, yet reports 872 nonresident recipients (average $5,837), and nonresident first-year aid applicants file FIU's own aid form (CDS H7); FIU's admissions pages describe only merit awards for international students. FIU's first-year merit scholarships (Gold and Blue Scholarships, $4,000 to $24,000 over four years for non-Florida residents, and non-resident out-of-state tuition waivers) are awarded automatically on the admissions application; the page says international students who receive an F-1 visa are eligible and funding is limited. Non-Florida-resident National Merit Finalists are funded by FIU (100% tuition and fees plus a book stipend, and housing with a meal plan). International students are directed to the Academic Works scholarship database and the Florida Linkage programs; the international cost page lists no need-based aid.
